sentences.text: Kodimyala Anjaiah, vs The State Of Telangana on 23 February,

2023 
Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili
 And
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik
 W.P.No.1745 Of 2023
Order:

(per AKS,J) Sri Kodimyala Anjaiah, the petitioner, has filed this Habeas Corpus petition on behalf of his son, Kodimyala Harikrishna @ Hareesh, the detenu, challenging the detention order vide Rc.No:C1/986/JGL/2022, dated 03.09.2022, passed by the respondent No.2, whereby, the detenu was detained under Section 3(2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers,
Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (as amended by Act No.13 of 2018) (for short, 'Act 1 of 1986'), and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.2064, dated 02.11.2022, passed by the 1st respondent.
2.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Heard Sri Baglekar Akash Kumar and Sri Cheekati Satish, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S. Mujib Kumar, learned Special Government Pleader, representing the learned Advocate General appearing for the respondents.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that petitioner's son was detained by invoking the provisions of the Act 1 of 1986 vide order dated 03.09.2022 on the ground that petitioner's son was involved in four crimes i.e., Cr.Nos.75, 76, 77 & 78 of 2022 for the offences punishable under Sections 376(AB), 506, 354-D IPC and Section 5 read with 6, Section 3 read with 4, Section 12 of POCSO Act, 2012 of Gollapalli Police Station.

Learned counsel had further contended that the detenu was arrested in pursuance of registration of the said crimes on 11.04.2022 and the petitioner's son is still languishing in jail as an under-trial prisoner.

Learned counsel has drawn attention of this Court to Section 3 of the Act, which reads as under:
3.Power to make orders detaining certain persons: (1) The Government may, if satisfied with respect to any boot-legger, dacoit, drug offender, goonda, immoral traffic offender (Land- Kodimyala Anjaiah, vs The State Of Telangana on 23 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131517640/
1 Grabber, Spurious Seed Offender, Insecticide Offender, Fertilizer Offender, Food Adulteration Offender, Fake Document Offender, Scheduled Commodities Offender, Forest Offender, Gaming Offender, Sexual Offender, Explosive Substances Offender, Arms Offender, Cyber Crime Offender and White Collar or Financial Offender) that with a view to preventing him from acting in any manner prejudicial to the maintenance of public order, it is necessary so to do, make an order directing that such person be detained.

(2) If, having regard to the circumstances prevailing or likely to prevail in any area within the local limits of the jurisdiction of a District Magistrate or a Commissioner of Police, the Government are satisfied that it is necessary so to do, they may, by order in writing, direct that during such period as may be specified in the order, such District Magistrate or Commissioner of Police may also, if satisfied as provided in sub-section (1), exercise the powers conferred by the said sub-section.

Provided that the period specified in the order made by the Government under this sub-section shall not in the first instance, exceed three months, but the Government may, if satisfied as aforesaid that it is necessary so to do, amend such order to extend such period from time to time by any period not exceeding three months at any one time.

(3) When any order is made under this section by an officer mentioned in sub-section (2), he shall forthwith report the fact to the Government together with the grounds on which the order has been made and such other particulars as in his opinion, have a bearing on the matter and no such order shall remain in force for more than twelve days after the making thereof, unless, in the meantime, it has been approved by the Government."

Learned counsel had further contended that the said section would make it clear that as on the date of detention, the authority which is passing the detention orders must be satisfied that the detenu must be detained by taking into consideration the factors which are prelevant as on the date of passing the detention orders.

Admittedly as on 03.09.2022 the date on which the detention order was passed, the petitioner's son was not disturbing the public nor the public were being effected with the detenu's presence in the society which would mean that the respondents have passed the impugned detention order without examining the case of the detenu as to whether it was detrimental to the society or public at large.

Learned counsel had further contended that admittedly the detenu is in judicial custody as an under trial prisoner from 11.04.2022 and when the detenu is in prison, there is no question of disturbing the public or public peace and therefore, the detention order is liable to be set aside.
4.

Learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents had contended that the detenu was involving in the offences which are grave in nature and that too against the minor children and that is the reason why the respondents have passed the detention order on 03.09.2022.

Therefore, there are no merits in the writ petition and the same is liable to be dismissed.
5.

Having considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel on either side, this Court is of the view that the respondents have passed the detention order on 03.09.2022 without application of mind as admittedly, the detenu is in prison as an under-trial prisoner from 11.04.2022 and hence,
the question of detenu disturbing the public peace or public at large does not arise.
Therefore, the detention order passed against the detenu is liable to be set aside.
6. Accordingly, the Writ Petition is allowed and the detention order dated 03.09.2022 passed against the detenu is set aside.

However, it is made clear that the detenu would not be set at free as Kodimyala Anjaiah, vs The State Of Telangana on 23 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131517640/
2 he is an under-trial prisoner.

sentences.text: It is always open for the respondents to invoke the provisions of the Act 1 of 1986 if the detenu is released and still disturbing the public at large.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
